label: Q8_0 single-row MMVQ t128_vdr2 — combined occupancy + ILP, default-on
rationale: C9's standalone t128 lost decisively to vdr2 because it threw away the ILP win (one DP4A per slot vs vdr2's two). C9-followup keeps the vdr2 inner-loop pattern and combines it with t128's 2-blocks-per-CU occupancy advantage. Sweep cert green (15 shapes via `flambeau sweep --op qmatmul --dtype Q8_0_t128_vdr2`).
wiring: qmatmul.rs dispatch: alias `qmatmul_q8_0_mmvq_single_row_gfx906` and `qmatmul_q8_0_mmvq_dp4a_vdr2_gfx906` to `qmatmul_q8_0_mmvq_t128_vdr2_gfx906` by default. Opt-out via FLAMBEAU_Q8_0_MMVQ_T128_VDR2=off.

results.note: Third vdr2 run was a cold-cache outlier (21.61 vs 24+); using best-of-3 as the comparison baseline gives the conservative +3.4 % delta.

decision.rationale: Stable +3 % across multi-run on both 27B-Q8_0 variants, bit-exact decode trajectory preserved, kernel is a pure superset of the existing vdr2 pattern. Initial C9 NULL was a single-run cold-cache outlier that mis-attributed t128's effect — multi-run reveals t128_vdr2 is the productisation winner.

diagnosis.why_c9_alone_lost: vdr2 amortizes per-thread ILP via a 2-DP4A inner loop. Plain t128 halves threads but keeps VDR=1, throwing away the ILP win.
diagnosis.why_c9_followup_wins: vdr2's per-thread ILP × t128's 2-blocks-per-CU latency hiding compose multiplicatively — neither lever alone matches the combined effect.

follow_ups.summary: mmvq_q8_0_gate_up_t128_vdr2 — apply the same combined lever to the fused gate+up Q8_0 kernel (currently 256t default). Q8_0 dense FFN gate+up is one of the per-layer call pairs that should also benefit from the same lever combo.
